newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep Archer says capital gains tax cut a must.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep Archer says capital gains tax cut a must.

text.p: The chairman of the House tax-writing committee said Wednesday a broad-based capital gains tax cut must ultimately be part of any agreement reached between congressional Republicans and the White House.

"They will not get a bill passed through the House without a broad-based capital gains relief," House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, said in an interview off the House floor.
"We understand that education tax relief is important to them (the administration)," and Republicans would negotiate on that front, he added, but did not give any specifics.

Archer said revenue raisers in the form of loophole closers and base broadeners should not exceed $5 billion over five years. That figure excluded the airline ticket tax, which is expected to raise about $30 billion over five years.
"I do not believe we can raise revenues in excess of $5 billion over five years," he said.
Clinton's budget proposed tax cuts of $98 billion over five years partly offset by tax increases of $76 billion, leaving a net tax cut of about $22 billion.
Archer said he had given some parameters on taxes to the House Budget Committee, but would not be more specific.
"It's clear to everyone we're going to have to have child (tax) credit, capital gains (tax cut), death tax relief," he said.
